review.why: The supplied creative remains the major source object, with a distinct, native-size financial commitment beside it. Its $4 customer offer is clearly separate from the $25.00 creator payment, whose conditions remain explicit. The later production frame demonstrates actual proof submission and a literal review state rather than implying acceptance or earnings. Typography, neutral surfaces, restrained controls and the source-to-terms relationship retain Frame Shift despite the intentionally different public-page composition. The two composite views show an occupied product stage, not a missing Lab assembly. Small embedded operational text has a clearly labeled external inspection route. Nothing visible establishes a functional regression or a release-blocking visual defect.
review.verdict: Frame Shift is faithfully carried into this desktop Post chapter, with coherent real-product storytelling and no visible release-blocking drift.
